title: Getting Started with tidybiome: A Modern, Tidyverse-Native Microbiome Suite
text: Downstream microbiome analysis historically divided legacy packages like phyloseq complex Bioconductor frameworks like mia / TreeSummarizedExperiment. powerful, tools often require navigating intricate S4 slots, rely outdated heuristics (arbitrary rarefaction pseudocount-based CLR), output visuals hard--read 50-color legends. tidybiome brings microbiome data science directly modern tidyverse ecosystem. acts lightweight, aesthetic Swiss Army knife built around following core principles: Native Tidyverse Ergonomics: tidy_microbiome container inherits tbl_df. Standard dplyr verbs (filter, mutate, select, arrange, slice) work seamlessly sample metadata keeping count matrices, taxonomic lineages, distance caches, phylogenetic trees synchronized hood. Robust CLR (rCLR): Zero-safe compositional normalization without pseudocount distortion (Martino et al., 2019). Unified Hill Numbers Profile: Richness (q=0q=0), exponential Shannon (q=1q=1), inverse Simpson (q=2q=2) intuitive scale effective number species. Phylogenetic UniFrac: High-performance vectorized unweighted weighted UniFrac distances via ancestor-descendant matrix algebra. Consensus Differential Abundance: Robust multi-engine consensus (LinDA, CAFT zero-cell separation, CLR-linear models, Wilcoxon) formula specification (formula = ~ treatment + age + batch), covariate adjustments, Cauchy combination testing. Constrained Ordination & Networks: Distance-based Redundancy Analysis (db-RDA) microbial co-occurrence networks false discovery rate (FDR) control degree centrality. Publication-Grade Visualizations: Soft-gray "" pooling, colorblind-safe palettes (Okabe-Ito, Nature), confidence ellipses, theme_tidybiome().

title: Statistical Rigor and Ecological Modeling in tidybiome
text: Microbiome data present profound statistical challenges: 1. Extreme Sparsity: High percentages true structural zero counts. 2. Compositionality: Sequencing yields relative proportions constrained simplex, shifts one taxon artificially inflate deflate others. 3. High Dimensionality: Hundreds thousands taxa small sample cohorts (P≫NP \gg N). 4. Confounding Covariates: Age, sex, antibiotic history, batch effects, sequencing depth bias naive comparisons. vignette explains tidybiome addresses challenges using modern statistical methods, formula-based linear modeling, phylogenetic distance vectorization, ecological modeling.

title: Statistical Rigor and Ecological Modeling in tidybiome
text: classical Centered Log-Ratio (CLR) transform defined : clr(xi)=[logxi1g(xi),…,logxiPg(xi)]\text{clr}(x_i) = \left[ \log\frac{x_{i1}}{g(x_i)}, \dots, \log\frac{x_{iP}}{g(x_i)} \right] g(xi)=(∏j=1Pxij)1/Pg(x_i) = (\prod_{j=1}^P x_{ij})^{1/P} geometric mean across taxa. microbiome data contain many zeros, analysts traditionally add arbitrary pseudocount: log⁡(xij+c)\log(x_{ij} + c) c∈{0.5,1}c \\{0.5, 1\}. However, demonstrated Martino et al. (2019), choice cc introduces severe mathematical artifacts: - Artificially alters sample geometric means. - Biases sample distance calculations ordination projections. - Generates spurious differential abundance biomarkers.

title: Statistical Rigor and Ecological Modeling in tidybiome
text: tidybiome implements rCLR, calculates geometric mean strictly observed non-zero counts: g>0(xi)=(∏j:xij>0xij)1/|{j:xij>0}|g_{>0}(x_i) = \left( \prod_{j: x_{ij} > 0} x_{ij} \right)^{1 / |\{j: x_{ij} > 0\}|} non-zero taxa: rclr(xij)=log⁡xijg>0(xi)\text{rclr}(x_{ij}) = \log\frac{x_{ij}}{g_{>0}(x_i)} zero counts (xij=0x_{ij} = 0), rclr(xij)\text{rclr}(x_{ij}) remains 0 without imputation distortion:
code: library(tidybiome) data("gut_microbiome", package = "tidybiome")  tb_rclr <- transform_abundance(gut_microbiome, method = "rclr") # Zero values in raw counts remain exactly zero in rclr raw_counts <- assay(tb_rclr, "counts") rclr_counts <- assay(tb_rclr, "rclr")  all(rclr_counts[raw_counts == 0] == 0) #> [1] TRUE

text: Zero-cell dropout probability via logistic regression: logit(P(Y=0))∼𝐗𝛃\text{logit}(P(Y=0)) \sim \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\beta} Abundance shifts among present counts via log-linear regression: log⁡(Y∣Y>0)∼𝐗𝛄\log(Y \mid Y > 0) \sim \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\gamma} Combines likelihood ratio test statistics gracefully suppressing separation warnings. LinDA (Zhou et al., 2022): Compositional linear regression selecting robust reference taxon via mode/rank estimation, fully controlling model matrix covariates. CLR-Linear: Fits multiple linear regression models rCLR CLR transformed features. Cauchy Combination Aggregation: Combines pp-values across disparate statistical frameworks single unified consensus pp-value (padj_consensus), weighted engine agreement score.

title: Statistical Rigor and Ecological Modeling in tidybiome
text: Calculating UniFrac traditionally requires deep recursive traversals tree every pair samples (O(N2⋅nodes)O(N^2 \cdot \text{nodes})), leading many R packages rely external C/C++ libraries. tidybiome implements vectorized algorithm using edge-descendant incidence matrix 𝐌∈{0,1}E×T\mathbf{M} \\{0, 1\}^{E \times T}, EE number edges tree TT number tips. tip traced root single precomputation step (O(T⋅depth)O(T \cdot \text{depth})). Multiplying: 𝐖=𝐌×𝐏\mathbf{W} = \mathbf{M} \times \mathbf{P} 𝐏∈[0,1]T×N\mathbf{P} \[0, 1]^{T \times N} sample proportion matrix, computes total descendant branch weight edges across NN samples simultaneously pure R matrix algebra.

title: Statistical Rigor and Ecological Modeling in tidybiome
text: Unweighted UniFrac: dunifrac(,B)=∑ele|𝕀(WeA>0)−𝕀(WeB>0)|∑ele𝕀(WeA+WeB>0)d_{\text{unifrac}}(, B) = \frac{\sum_e l_e |\mathbb{}(W_{eA} > 0) - \mathbb{}(W_{eB} > 0)|}{\sum_e l_e \mathbb{}(W_{eA} + W_{eB} > 0)} Weighted Normalized UniFrac: dwunifrac(,B)=∑ele|WeA−WeB|∑ele(WeA+WeB)d_{\text{wunifrac}}(, B) = \frac{\sum_e l_e |W_{eA} - W_{eB}|}{\sum_e l_e (W_{eA} + W_{eB})}
code: taxa_ids <- attr(gut_microbiome, "tax_table")$taxon_id set.seed(123) tree <- ape::rtree(length(taxa_ids), tip.label = taxa_ids) tb_phylo <- set_tree(gut_microbiome, tree)  # Fast vectorized calculations: dist_unweighted <- calc_unifrac(tb_phylo, weighted = FALSE) dist_weighted   <- calc_unifrac(tb_phylo, weighted = TRUE, normalized = TRUE)  as.matrix(dist_unweighted)[1:3, 1:3] #>            Sample_01  Sample_02  Sample_03 #> Sample_01 0.00000000 0.09757923 0.03646537 #> Sample_02 0.09757923 0.00000000 0.06182808 #> Sample_03 0.03646537 0.06182808 0.00000000 as.matrix(dist_weighted)[1:3, 1:3] #>            Sample_01  Sample_02  Sample_03 #> Sample_01 0.00000000 0.06479822 0.01380644 #> Sample_02 0.06479822 0.00000000 0.06485739 #> Sample_03 0.01380644 0.06485739 0.00000000

title: Transform Abundance Data Using Compositional or Classical Normalization — transform_abundance
text: tb tidy_microbiome object. method Character string specifying transformation method. Options: "rclr": Robust Centered Log-Ratio (Martino et al. 2019). Zero values remain zero; positive values centered geometric mean observed (non-zero) taxa. "clr": Classic Centered Log-Ratio pseudocount. "relabundance": Total Sum Scaling (TSS), scaling sample sum 1. "coverage": Coverage-based standardization using Good-Turing sample coverage. "hellinger": Hellinger transformation (square root relative abundance). "gmpr": Geometric Mean Pairwise Ratios (Chen et al. 2018), zero-tolerant size-factor normalization. "log10": Log10 transformation pseudocount. "pa": Presence/Absence binary transformation (0 1). assay Character string naming source assay transform. Defaults "counts". name Optional character string naming output assay. Defaults method. pseudocount Numeric pseudocount added "clr" "log10". Defaults 1. min_overlap Minimum number shared non-zero taxa required GMPR pairwise ratios (default: 2).
